subtopic: Planning a trip on a budget
subtype: Approach: involving parents and choosing safe arrangements [Action]
passage:
In the school staffroom on Friday, Himani laid a printed sheet in front of Arnab Sir and the six parents who had come. “Leaving at 6:10, reaching the hostel by 5. Here are the hostel's name, address and phone. Here are all our contact numbers.” Her father looked up. “And check-ins?”
“Every evening at eight, one call from the group leader to the parent list, plus a message when we reach and when we leave.”
Arnab Sir added, “I'm travelling with them, and Ms Roy will be the second adult.”
The parents asked about the return train, and Himani had the number and the timing. One mother said she would sleep easier. The list was signed, and each parent kept a copy.

qa.q: When will the group leader call the parents each evening?
qa.a: The group leader will call every evening at eight.

qa.q: What is Himani feeling as she lays out the sheet?
qa.a: Himani seems nervous but prepared, since she has every detail ready and answers each question clearly.

qa.q: What could the group do if an evening call is missed?
qa.a: They could keep a backup contact, such as Arnab Sir's number, so parents can reach an adult, and agree on what to do when a check-in is late.

qa.q: How might a parent feel after seeing the sheet?
qa.a: One mother says she would sleep easier, so parents feel reassured by the details and the adults travelling along.

grounding: Teens share the itinerary, hostel details and contact numbers with parents, agree check-in times and travel with a responsible adult.
